# Species contributions (Q4)

<!-- readme-only -->

**What and why.** The observed movement of a community between t1 and t2 is the sum of one
vector per species: the change in the species' share times the species' fixed position in the
CCA plane. Projecting each species' vector on a reference direction says how much that species
moved the community along it. Two measures are used, both per century. Along the direction the
prediction moved (`contrib_climate`), a positive value means the species carried the community with
the climate. The second measure, `contrib_lag`, splits the lag rate itself. The mismatch g, from the
predicted to the observed position, is taken at both ends (g1 at t1, g2 at t2), and m is their sum
divided by the sum of their lengths. Each species' vector projected on m is that species' part of the
lag rate, and the predicted movement projected on m, with its sign reversed, is the climate's part.
Because the change in mismatch, g2 − g1, is the observed movement minus the predicted movement, and
(g2 − g1)·m is exactly the change in the length of the mismatch, the species parts and the climate
part add up exactly to the lag rate (asserted). A negative species value means the species narrowed
the lag, a positive value that it widened it. Swapping the two surveys reverses every value, so the
measure has no direction of its own. It replaces `contrib_gap`, the projection on the mismatch at
the start alone. That measure leaned positive: a community sampled away from its predicted position
tends to come back towards it by chance, and run backwards in time it also appeared to close the
gap. `contrib_lag` is per century of the same interval as the lag rate.

**How it is calculated.**

```{r step6-code}
code_snippet('R/helpers/cca_transition_contributions.R', 'contrib-lag')
code_snippet('R/pipeline/16_contributions.R', 'species-means')
```

**Result.**

<!-- /readme-only -->

```{r step6-results}
species_means = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_means.csv')
species_means |> mutate(value = ifelse(interval_defined, sprintf('%+.3f (%.3f to %.3f)', estimate, conf_low, conf_high),
    ifelse(present, sprintf('%+.3f', estimate), 'absent'))) |>
  select(measure, species, site, period_type, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(measure, period_type), values_from = value) |>
  rename(Species = species, Park = site) |>
  show_table('step6_species_means', caption = paste('**Table S23. Species contributions per century.** Mean and 95% confidence',
    'interval (t-interval) in CCA distance per century, for each species, park, and period type. The columns give the measure and',
    'the period type: contrib_climate, how far the species moved the community in the climate-predicted direction (positive) or',
    'against it (negative); contrib_lag, the part of the lag rate that is due to the species (positive values amplify the lag, and',
    'negative values shrink it). "absent": the species was not found in that park and period type. contrib_lag includes the',
    'lake-periods and plot pairs in which the community did not move (all species at zero), and contrib_climate does not.'))
lag_parts = read_output('cca_transition_contributions/lag_decomposition.csv')
tci = function(x) { n = length(x); m = mean(x); h = qt(.975, n - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(n)
  sprintf('%+.3f (%+.3f to %+.3f)', m, m - h, m + h) }
lag_parts |> mutate(period_type = factor(period_type, levels = c('Holocene-S', 'Holocene-C', 'Anthropocene'))) |>
  group_by(Park = site, `Period type` = period_type) |>
  summarise(Units = n(), `Lag rate` = tci(lag_rate), `Species (sum)` = tci(species_sum),
    `Climate part` = tci(climate_part), .groups = 'drop') |>
  show_table('step6_lag_decomposition', caption = paste('**Table S24. The lag rate divided into the part due to the species and the part',
    'due to climate.** Means over the lake-periods or plot pairs with 95% confidence intervals (t-intervals), in CCA distance per',
    'century. In each lake-period and plot pair, the contributions of all species and the part due to climate add up to the lag',
    'rate. Positive values amplify the lag, and negative values shrink it.'))
```

<!-- readme-only -->

The species vectors add up to the observed movement for every lake-period and plot pair (asserted).
```{r step6-numbers}
hol = species_means |> filter(period_type != 'Anthropocene')
hol_away = hol |> filter(interval_defined, conf_low > 0 | conf_high < 0)
lag_species = species_means |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene', measure == 'contrib_lag', interval_defined)
lp = lag_parts |> filter(era == 'Anthropocene') |> group_by(site) |>
  summarise(lag = mean(lag_rate), species = mean(species_sum), climate = mean(climate_part))
lpv = function(p, v) sprintf('%+.2f', lp[[v]][lp$site == p])
narrow = lag_species |> filter(conf_high < 0); widen = lag_species |> filter(conf_low > 0)
r_measures = species_means |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene') |>
  select(measure, species, site, estimate) |> pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = estimate) |>
  group_by(site) |> summarise(r = cor(contrib_climate, contrib_lag, use = 'complete.obs'))
```

In the Holocene every species mean is close to zero in both parks (largest absolute value
`r sprintf('%.3f', max(abs(hol$estimate)))` CCA distance per century).
`r if (nrow(hol_away)) paste0(nrow(hol_away), ' of ', sum(hol$interval_defined), ' Holocene intervals exclude zero (',
paste(sprintf('%s, %s, %s, %s', hol_away$species, hol_away$site, hol_away$period_type, hol_away$measure), collapse = '; '),
'), all smaller than ', sprintf('%.3f', max(abs(hol_away$estimate))), ' in absolute value.') else
paste0('None of the ', sum(hol$interval_defined), ' Holocene intervals excludes zero.')` The Anthropocene
means are larger.

In the Anthropocene the climate's part of the lag rate is about the same in both parks
(`r lpv('MORA', 'climate')` at MORA, `r lpv('NOCA', 'climate')` at NOCA, CCA distance per century): the
predicted positions moved away from the communities. The parks differ in their species. At MORA the
species added to the lag (sum `r lpv('MORA', 'species')`), so the lag rate was `r lpv('MORA', 'lag')`. At
NOCA they narrowed it by more than the climate widened it (sum `r lpv('NOCA', 'species')`), so the lag
rate was `r lpv('NOCA', 'lag')`. Species whose interval lies below zero, which narrowed the lag:
`r paste(sprintf('%s (%s, %+.3f)', narrow$species, narrow$site, narrow$estimate), collapse = ', ')`.
Species whose interval lies above zero, which widened it:
`r paste(sprintf('%s (%s, %+.3f)', widen$species, widen$site, widen$estimate), collapse = ', ')`.
Across species the two measures are negatively correlated in the Anthropocene
(r = `r sprintf('%.2f', r_measures$r[r_measures$site == 'MORA'])` at MORA,
`r sprintf('%.2f', r_measures$r[r_measures$site == 'NOCA'])` at NOCA): species that moved the community with the
climate-predicted direction narrowed the lag, and those that moved it against that direction widened
it.

```{r step6-contrasts}
sc = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_contrasts.csv')
sc_sig = sc |> filter(p_adjusted < .05)
```

The period types of a species are compared with Welch tests, three contrasts per species, measure and
park, and the p-values are Holm-adjusted within each measure and park across all species and
contrasts. Of `r sum(!is.na(sc$p_value))` testable contrasts, `r sum(sc$p_value < .05, na.rm = TRUE)` have
p < 0.05 before the adjustment and `r nrow(sc_sig)` after it
(`r paste(sprintf('%s %s, %s, %s', sc_sig$species, sc_sig$site, sc_sig$contrast, sc_sig$measure), collapse = '; ')`).
`r if (nrow(sc_sig) && all(startsWith(sc_sig$contrast, 'Anthropocene'))) 'All of them set the Anthropocene against a Holocene period type.' else ''`

```{r fig-8-main}
show_figure('report/figures/main/fig_species_contributions.pdf')
```

**Fig. 8. Species contributions in the Holocene and the Anthropocene.** Each species' vector is its
change in share between the first and the last sampled century of a lake-period, or between the
legacy survey and the resurvey of a plot, times its fixed position in the CCA plane. The upper row (following climate-predicted direction)
projects these vectors on the direction in which the climate-predicted position moved, and the lower
row (changing the climate-community lag) on the average direction of the mismatch at the two ends, so
that the species' values plus the climate's part add up to the lag rate. Labels at the top of each panel read with the row title: a species moved the community following or against the climate-predicted direction (upper row), and narrowed or widened the climate-community lag (lower row). The lower row includes the lake-periods and plot pairs whose composition did not change (all species values zero) and is per century of the same interval as the lag rate.
Species are ordered by the maximum elevation of the plots where they occur (the 605 plot pairs, both surveys, both parks), the highest at the top. Their names are shaded by that maximum in four grey steps, lightest below 1,500 m and black above 1,900 m (key below the figure). Names in bold are species absent from the Holocene record of both parks.
Symbols are means: triangles, Holocene stability periods, circles, Holocene climate-change periods,
diamonds, Anthropocene plot pairs (burned and unburned together). Large symbols with bars are means whose
95% t-interval excludes zero, small faded symbols are means whose interval includes zero. A species with no
Holocene symbols in a park is absent from that park's Holocene record.
Each park has its own x scale, symmetric around zero. `r both_spans` Contributions are in CCA distance per century.

<!-- /readme-only -->

**Species contributions not divided by time.** Per century, the species contributions of the Holocene are
small partly because the lake-periods are long, and those of the Anthropocene are large partly because the
time between the two surveys is short. We therefore also calculated them without dividing by time
(Fig. S15, Table S25).

```{r step6-totals}
st = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_means_total.csv')
stc = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_contrasts_total.csv')
dts = read_output('cca_transition_contributions/species_contributions.csv') |>
  distinct(era, site, series, unit_index, plot_id, vegetation_dt_years) |>
  group_by(era) |> summarise(lo = min(vegetation_dt_years), hi = max(vegetation_dt_years))
dr = function(e) sprintf('%s to %s', prettyNum(dts$lo[dts$era == e], big.mark = ','),
  prettyNum(dts$hi[dts$era == e], big.mark = ','))
# Means whose 95% interval excludes zero, for species present in that park and period type.
away = function(d) d |> filter(present, interval_defined, conf_low > 0 | conf_high < 0)
key = function(d) sort(paste(d$measure, d$species, d$site))
hol_t = st |> filter(period_type != 'Anthropocene', present)
hol_r = species_means |> filter(period_type != 'Anthropocene', present)
top = hol_t |> slice_max(abs(estimate), n = 1)
ant_t = away(st |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene'))
ant_r = away(species_means |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene'))
show_figure('report/figures/supplementary/figS15_species_contributions_total.pdf')
```

The Holocene lake-periods span `r dr('Holocene')` years and the Anthropocene plot pairs `r dr('Anthropocene')`
years. Not divided by time, a species contribution is how far the species moved the community between t1
and t2. The mean contributions of the Holocene were then as large as those of the Anthropocene (the largest
was *`r top$species`* at `r top$site`, `r top$period_type`, `r top$measure`, with `r sprintf('%+.3f', top$estimate)`
CCA distance). However, they varied so much among the few lake-periods that the confidence interval
excluded zero for `r nrow(away(hol_t))` of the `r sum(hol_t$interval_defined)` Holocene means
(`r nrow(away(hol_r))` per century). In the Anthropocene, the confidence interval excluded zero for
`r nrow(ant_t)` means, against `r nrow(ant_r)` per century, `r if (identical(key(ant_t), key(ant_r))) 'for the same species in the same parks' else 'not all for the same species'`.
After adjustment with the Holm method, `r sum(stc$p_adjusted < .05, na.rm = TRUE)` of the `r sum(!is.na(stc$p_value))`
differences between period types were significant, against `r nrow(sc_sig)` per century. Thus, the large
species contributions per century in the Anthropocene come mainly from changes that took place within a few
decades. Within a lake-period, the species of the Holocene moved the communities about as far, but too
variably among lake-periods to identify which species did so.

**Fig. S15. Species contributions not divided by time.** As Fig. 8 of the main text, with the contribution
of each species between t1 and t2 and not per century. Upper row: how far each species moved the community
in the climate-predicted direction (positive values) or against it (negative values). Lower row: how far
each species moved the community away from its climate-predicted position, which is the part of the lag
that is due to that species. Means with 95% confidence intervals (t-intervals). Symbols, order of the
species, and shading as in Fig. 8. `r both_spans` Contributions are in CCA distance.

```{r step6-totals-table}
st |> mutate(value = ifelse(interval_defined, sprintf('%+.3f (%.3f to %.3f)', estimate, conf_low, conf_high),
    ifelse(present, sprintf('%+.3f', estimate), 'absent'))) |>
  select(measure, species, site, period_type, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(measure, period_type), values_from = value) |>
  rename(Species = species, Park = site) |>
  show_table('step6_species_means_total', caption = paste('**Table S25. Species contributions not divided by time.** Mean',
    'and 95% confidence interval (t-interval) in CCA distance, for each species, park, and period type. Columns as in Table S23.'))
```

# Appendix S4. The analysis with a partial correction and without correction of the Holocene climate

```{r appendix-s4-setup}
s4_dir = here::here('output_paleoclimate_sensitivity', 'comparison')
s4_has = file.exists(file.path(s4_dir, 'explanatory_slopes.csv'))
s4_term_label = c(siteNOCA = 'Site (NOCA minus MORA)', climate_rate = 'Climate change rate',
  climate_change = 'Climate change', fire_activity = 'Fire activity')
s4_run = c(two_step = 'two-step (main)', one_step = 'one-step', raw = 'raw')
s4_p = function(p) ifelse(p < .001, '< 0.001', sprintf('%.3f', p))
s4_read = function(f) readr::read_csv(file.path(s4_dir, f), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

The bias correction of the Holocene climate (Appendix S2) assumes that the difference between the climate
products was constant through the Holocene. To assess how much the results depend on this correction, we
repeated the analysis, from the Holocene climate onwards, with two other versions of the Holocene climate:
with the one-step correction (step 2 alone, i.e., CHELSAcruts to CHELSA V2.1), and without correction. Among
the three analyses, only the climate-predicted positions of the Holocene communities and the climate
periods can change. The observed positions do not change, and neither do community turnover and all
quantities of the Anthropocene. We compared the lake-periods that the three analyses have in common, i.e.,
those with the same lake, period type, t1, and t2 (Fig. S16, Table S20), the differences between period
types (see Table S16 for the main analysis), and the associations with climate change and fire in the
Holocene (Fig. S17).<!-- readme-only --> [`R/sensitivity_paleoclimate.R`](R/sensitivity_paleoclimate.R) reruns stages 08 to 16 twice into
`output_paleoclimate_sensitivity/` and leaves the main outputs untouched. The raw TraCE21k was the
paleoclimate of the analysis until 11 November 2026. The counts below are read from the tables that the
script writes to `output_paleoclimate_sensitivity/comparison/`.<!-- /readme-only -->

```{r appendix-s4-figure}
if (s4_has) {
  s4_match = s4_read('lake_period_matching.csv')
  # Whether the three runs drew the same climate periods (same names, types and ends).
  s4_periods = s4_read('climate_periods.csv') |> select(run, period, period_type, older_cal_bp, younger_cal_bp)
  s4_catalog = split(select(s4_periods, -run), s4_periods$run)
  s4_same_periods = all(vapply(s4_catalog, \(x) isTRUE(all.equal(as.data.frame(x), as.data.frame(s4_catalog$two_step),
    check.attributes = FALSE)), logical(1)))
  s4_lp = s4_read('lake_period_responses.csv')
  s4_kept = function(r, p, other) { x = s4_lp |> filter(response == r, site == p, is.finite(two_step), is.finite(.data[[other]]))
    sprintf('%d of %d', sum(sign(x$two_step) == sign(x[[other]])), nrow(x)) }
  s4_change = function(run) { x = s4_lp |> filter(response == 'climate_change', raw > 0)
    sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * median(abs(x[[run]] / x$raw - 1))) }
  s4_r = s4_read('lake_period_correlations.csv')
  s4_r1 = function(resp, park, run) sprintf('%.2f', s4_r$r[s4_r$response == resp & s4_r$site == park & s4_r$run == run])
  s4_tracking = c('lag', 'lag_rate', 'pace_effect_total', 'pace_effect', 'direction_effect_total', 'direction_effect')
  s4_rr = function(park, run) { x = s4_r |> filter(site == park, run == .env$run, response %in% s4_tracking)
    sprintf('%.2f to %.2f', min(x$r), max(x$r)) }
  s4_ec = s4_read('era_contrasts.csv')
  s4_sig = function(run) sum(s4_ec[[paste0('p_adjusted_', run)]] < .05)
  s4_ec_changed = s4_ec |> filter((p_adjusted_two_step < .05) != (p_adjusted_one_step < .05) |
    (p_adjusted_two_step < .05) != (p_adjusted_raw < .05))
  s4_sl = s4_read('explanatory_slopes.csv')
  s4_away = function(run) sum(s4_sl[[paste0('conf_low_', run)]] > 0 | s4_sl[[paste0('conf_high_', run)]] < 0)
  s4_sl_main = s4_sl |> filter(conf_low_two_step > 0 | conf_high_two_step < 0)
  show_figure('report/figures/supplementary/figS16_paleoclimate_lake_periods.pdf', width = '75%')
} else cat('Run Rscript R/sensitivity_paleoclimate.R to fill this appendix.\n')
```

**Fig. S16. Holocene lake-periods with and without correction of the Holocene climate.** Each point is one
lake-period that the three analyses have in common, with its value without correction (x-axis) against its
value with the two-step correction of the main analysis (red) and with the one-step correction (grey), each
with its least-squares line: (A) climate change and (B) its rate, (C) the lag and (D) its rate, (E) the pace
effect and (F) its rate, (G) the direction effect and (H) its rate. Left: quantities between t1 and t2. Right:
their rates per century. Circles are MORA and triangles NOCA. On the dashed line, a correction changes
nothing, and in the shaded quadrants, the value changes sign. The numbers in each panel are the Pearson
correlations (r), across the lake-periods of each park, between each corrected analysis and the analysis
without correction. Lake-periods in which the observed or the climate-predicted position did not move have
no pace or direction effect. Community turnover is the same in the three analyses and is not shown. Climate
change is in SD of the legacy plots, and the other quantities are in CCA distance (left) or in CCA distance
per century (right).<!-- readme-only --> Script:
[`R/figures/supp_paleoclimate_sensitivity.R`](R/figures/supp_paleoclimate_sensitivity.R).<!-- /readme-only -->

```{r appendix-s4-text, results = 'asis'}
if (s4_has) {
  s4_lst = function(d, f) if (nrow(d)) paste(f(d), collapse = '; ') else 'none'
  # Same sign as in the main analysis (two-step correction), for the era contrasts and the Holocene slopes.
  s4_same = function(d, run) sign(d[[paste0('estimate_', run)]]) == sign(d$estimate_two_step)
  s4_era = s4_ec |> filter(startsWith(contrast, 'Anthropocene'))
  s4_hol = s4_ec |> filter(!startsWith(contrast, 'Anthropocene'))
  s4_era_main = s4_era |> filter(p_adjusted_two_step < .05)
  s4_hol_main = s4_hol |> filter(p_adjusted_two_step < .05)
  # Significant with the same sign in another analysis.
  s4_robust = function(d, run) sum(s4_same(d, run) & d[[paste0('p_adjusted_', run)]] < .05)
  s4_era_flip = s4_era_main[!s4_same(s4_era_main, 'one_step') | !s4_same(s4_era_main, 'raw'), ]
  s4_against = c('Anthropocene - Holocene-C' = 'Anthropocene against Holocene climate-change periods',
    'Anthropocene - Holocene-S' = 'Anthropocene against Holocene stability periods')
  s4_sl_same = function(run) sum(s4_same(s4_sl_main, run))
  s4_sl_also = function(run) sum(s4_same(s4_sl_main, run) &
    (s4_sl_main[[paste0('conf_low_', run)]] > 0 | s4_sl_main[[paste0('conf_high_', run)]] < 0))
  # Lake-periods whose lag has the opposite sign in another analysis.
  s4_opposite = function(p, other) { x = s4_lp |> filter(response == 'lag', site == p, is.finite(two_step), is.finite(.data[[other]]))
    sprintf('%d of %d', sum(sign(x$two_step) != sign(x[[other]])), nrow(x)) }
  cat(paste0('**Lake-periods.** ',
    if (s4_same_periods) sprintf('The three analyses had the same %d climate periods (Table S6). ', nrow(s4_catalog$two_step)) else
      paste0('The three analyses had different climate periods (', paste(sprintf('%d with the %s Holocene climate',
        vapply(s4_catalog, nrow, integer(1)), s4_run[names(s4_catalog)]), collapse = '; '), '). '),
    if (all(s4_match$lake_periods == s4_match$shared_by_all[1])) sprintf('They also had the same %d lake-periods. ', s4_match$shared_by_all[1]) else
      paste0('They had ', s4_match$shared_by_all[1], ' lake-periods in common (', paste(sprintf('%d with the %s Holocene climate',
        s4_match$lake_periods, s4_run[s4_match$run]), collapse = '; '), '). '),
    'The climate change of a lake-period differed from that without correction by a median of ', s4_change('two_step'),
    ' with the two-step correction and of ', s4_change('one_step'), ' with the one-step correction (Fig. S16A, B). ',
    'The lag had the same sign in the main analysis and with the one-step correction in ', s4_kept('lag', 'MORA', 'one_step'),
    ' lake-periods at MORA and in ', s4_kept('lag', 'NOCA', 'one_step'), ' at NOCA. Without correction, it had the same sign as in the ',
    'main analysis in ', s4_kept('lag', 'MORA', 'raw'), ' lake-periods at MORA and in ', s4_kept('lag', 'NOCA', 'raw'),
    ' at NOCA (Fig. S16C, Table S20). Across the lake-periods, the lag, the pace effect, the direction effect, and their rates ',
    'in the main analysis were correlated with those without correction with r = ', s4_rr('MORA', 'two_step'), ' at MORA and ',
    s4_rr('NOCA', 'two_step'), ' at NOCA, and those with the one-step correction with r = ', s4_rr('MORA', 'one_step'), ' and ',
    s4_rr('NOCA', 'one_step'), '.\n\n',
    '**Differences between period types.** Of the ', nrow(s4_era), ' differences between the Anthropocene and a Holocene period ',
    'type (ten quantities, two parks, and two Holocene period types; Table S16), ', nrow(s4_era_main),
    ' were significant in the main analysis. Of these, ', s4_robust(s4_era_main, 'one_step'),
    ' were also significant, with the same sign, with the one-step correction, and ', s4_robust(s4_era_main, 'raw'),
    ' without correction. ',
    if (nrow(s4_era_flip)) paste0('The sign changed for: ', s4_lst(s4_era_flip, function(d) sprintf('%s at %s, %s',
      tolower(response_label[d$response]), d$site, s4_against[d$contrast])), '. ') else 'None of them changed sign. ',
    'Of the ', nrow(s4_hol), ' differences between the Holocene climate-change periods and the Holocene stability periods, ',
    nrow(s4_hol_main), ' were significant in the main analysis (', s4_lst(s4_hol_main, function(d) sprintf('%s at %s',
      tolower(response_label[d$response]), d$site)), '). Of these, ', s4_robust(s4_hol_main, 'one_step'),
    ' were also significant, with the same sign, with the one-step correction, and ', s4_robust(s4_hol_main, 'raw'),
    ' without correction.\n\n',
    '**Associations with climate change and fire in the Holocene.** Of the ', nrow(s4_sl), ' coefficients of park, climate change, ',
    'and fire activity in the Holocene models (Fig. S17), the confidence interval excluded zero for ', s4_away('two_step'),
    ' in the main analysis, for ', s4_away('one_step'), ' with the one-step correction, and for ', s4_away('raw'),
    ' without correction. Of the ', nrow(s4_sl_main), ' coefficients of the main analysis, ', s4_sl_same('one_step'),
    ' had the same sign with the one-step correction, and ', s4_sl_same('raw'), ' without correction: ',
    s4_lst(s4_sl_main, function(d) sprintf('%s, %s (%+.3f in the main analysis, %+.3f with the one-step correction, %+.3f without correction)',
      tolower(response_label[d$response]), tolower(s4_term_label[d$term]), d$estimate_two_step, d$estimate_one_step, d$estimate_raw)), '.\n\n',
    '**Consequences for the conclusions.** ',
    if (nrow(s4_era_flip) == 0) paste0('All differences between the Anthropocene and the Holocene that were significant in the main ',
      'analysis had the same sign in the three analyses. The comparison between the two eras therefore does not depend on the ',
      'correction of the Holocene climate. ') else paste0('Of the differences between the Anthropocene and the Holocene that were ',
      'significant in the main analysis, ', nrow(s4_era_flip), ' changed sign in one of the two other analyses. The comparison between ',
      'the two eras therefore depends in part on the correction of the Holocene climate. '),
    'The results that rest on the Holocene alone were less robust. Without correction, the lag had the opposite sign in ',
    s4_opposite('MORA', 'raw'), ' lake-periods at MORA and in ', s4_opposite('NOCA', 'raw'), ' at NOCA, ', s4_robust(s4_hol_main, 'raw'),
    ' of the ', nrow(s4_hol_main), ' significant differences between the Holocene climate-change and stability periods remained, and ',
    nrow(s4_sl_main) - s4_sl_same('raw'), ' of the ', nrow(s4_sl_main), ' Holocene coefficients changed sign. With the one-step ',
    'correction, ', s4_sl_same('one_step'), ' of these ', nrow(s4_sl_main), ' coefficients kept their sign, but the confidence interval ',
    'excluded zero for only ', s4_sl_also('one_step'), ' of them. We therefore interpret the lags of single lake-periods, the differences ',
    'within the Holocene, and the associations with climate change and fire in the Holocene with caution.\n'))
}
```

